precision-only.t: Two spam filters. By **precision alone**, Model A (**0.95**) looks much better than Model B (**0.75**).

recall-only.t: By **recall alone** the picture flips: Model B (**0.75**) finds far more spam than Model A (**0.40**). One metric can tell the opposite story to another.

imbalanced-pair.t: Model A is **very reliable when it flags** an email, but it **misses 60 percent** of the spam. It is a cautious filter.

balanced-pair.t: Model B is less precise but **finds far more spam**. Its two numbers are **balanced**.

need-combination.t: It depends on the goal. Often we want **one number that reflects both** precision and recall, so that models can be compared directly.

f1-formula.t: **F1 = 2 × (precision × recall) / (precision + recall).** It is the **harmonic mean** of precision and recall.

harmonic-balance.t: The ordinary average of 0.95 and 0.40 is **0.675**, but the harmonic mean is only **0.563**: it is pulled toward the smaller value. For the balanced pair both means are **0.75**.

calculate-example.t: Precision **0.667** and recall **0.80** give **F1 = 2 × 0.667 × 0.80 / 1.467 = 0.727**, slightly below the plain average of 0.733 and closer to the weaker number.

interpret.t: F1 is **high only when both are high** and falls if either is low. It treats precision and recall as equally important, so it is a common summary, **not the best metric for every problem**.
